blocking: [claude-fallback] The shell's CSP leaks into user code: C/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:58 renders user HTML "in an iframe as `srcdoc`", and line 63 says the shell must "Run under its own strict CSP". A `srcdoc` document inherits its embedder's policy container, so the shell's strict CSP applies to every user script. The injected inline shim (line 60) and users' inline scripts or remote fetches would be blocked unless the shell's CSP is loosened, and loosening it opens the injection surface on the session-bearing host that line 63 says must not exist. Built as written, either apps break or the shell's safety goal fails.

[claude-fallback] No handling of origin state left on the host that becomes trusted: stage 1 turns `<name>.plinth.example` into our session-bearing shell origin and relies on existing apps' data there (line 85 "apps already published today have data in their real `<name>.plinth.example` origin. That's the same origin the shell now runs on"). Any service worker an existing app registered on that origin keeps intercepting navigations and can replace the shell with top-level user code. The plan has no SW unregistration, `Clear-Site-Data`, or SW-script 404 rule, and the only release gate (lines 100-105) tests fresh apps. Line 79 also mentions service workers only as unavailable inside the frame.
